Hi Amy — great to hear ClearScale found the demo useful. Attached is a concise annual-commit playbook that maps Starter / Growth / Enterprise tiers to token commits, effective per-token pricing, and our overage & SLA safety options. High level summary inside the PDF and below. (attachment: Redwood_Annual_Commit_Proposal_v2.pdf (pdf, 118KB))

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Starter: 10M tokens/month commit (120M annual) — base rate $0.00065/token, 10% discount vs list. Best for small pilots with predictable traffic.
- Growth: 50M tokens/month commit (600M annual) — base rate $0.00050/token, 25% discount vs list. Includes 5% carryover pool and burst credits for 3× short bursts/month.
- Enterprise: 250M tokens/month commit (3B annual) — base rate $0.00035/token, 45% discount vs list. Includes 10% carryover pool, guaranteed reserved concurrency, and 99.9% monthly uptime SLA.

Key commercial knobs:
- SLA-linked discounts: if monthly SLOs (95th-percentile latency for p50/p95 targets we agree) are missed beyond the SLA window, customers receive a credit applied against next invoice (service credits scaled to severity). For Enterprise, repeated SLA misses trigger an incremental credit up to 5% of that month's committed spend.
- Overage safety: for committed tiers, overages billed at a lowered overage rate (e.g., Growth overage = base rate + 15% vs. list) rather than list rate. We also offer an automatic safety fallback: if committed capacity is saturated we route overflow to a compatible, lower-cost model variant to preserve availability (with flagged quality delta).
- Carryover and smoothing: Growth/Enterprise include a carryover pool (monthly accrual) to apply unused committed tokens to future months; unused carryover expires after 3 months.
- Early-exit & ramp: staged ramp schedule and partial refunds for first 90 days if traffic materially deviates from forecast (details in PDF).

If you want, I can shorten this into a one-page summary for procurement and push a DocuSign-ready contract with SLA addendum.

Next steps:
1) Tell me which tier you want us to price deeper (we can generate an exact ARR + credit table).
2) Confirm any specific p95 latency targets you need in the SLA.

Thanks — cc'ing procurement so they have the doc.

— Logan

Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:48:00 -07:00

Thanks Logan — the breakdown helps. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and our engineering lead:

1) Pricing: Growth sounds closest to our needs, but the per-token for Growth is still ~20% higher than what we're budgeting. Can you move Growth to $0.00042/token if we do a 12-month commit at the 50M/month level? We'd like a fixed invoice schedule and predictable CPI.

2) SLA credits: Procurement wants a stiffer SLA credit for P95 misses for customer-impacting incidents (e.g., 30+ minutes of degraded latency) — proposal: 10% credit for that month for each occurrence, capped at 20%/month. Is Redwood able to accept that in a contract?

3) Overage handling: We appreciate the fallback to a lower-cost model, but we need transparency: that fallback must be logged and visible in our console (flagged request IDs) and we need an opt-out (so our product team can choose to block fallback for critical flows).

4) DocuSign: We prefer to have the SLA addendum as part of the same envelope.

If we can get closer on pricing and agree the fallback transparency terms, procurement is ready to move.

Best,
Amy
Amy Carter
Director, Product — ClearScale

Proposed counter (short):
- Growth tier: accept 50M tokens/month @ $0.00042/token for a 12-month commit (ARR math in the PDF). Give procurement a fixed monthly invoice schedule and 30-day net terms.
- SLA credits: accept a modified SLA credit where customer receives 5% credit for month for each verified P95 customer-impacting incident >30 minutes, capped at 15%/month. Also include a remediation window and escalation path; 10%/month is above our standard tolerance without legal sign-off.
- Overage & fallback: keep the lower overage rate and automatic fallback but add: (a) fallback events are logged and surfaced in the Console with request IDs and model variant, (b) provide an opt-out toggle for any API key so certain routes are blocked from fallback (this will be a config change, may take 2 weeks to implement but we can ship a temporary "blocklist" rule earlier).
- DocuSign: include SLA addendum in same envelope; attach SLA-Addendum-Redwood.docx.

We'd need Marissa to approve the $0.00042 price (that's ~16% off our Growth base) and Dylan to confirm we can commit to visibility + opt-out. If you both sign off I'll package a one-page commercial summary and a DocuSign envelope.

Thanks,
